text_block: We pre-train the obstacle map network Gϕ first to attain robust obstacle map priors before joint optimization with the semantic map network ˜Gϕ(sτ, cτ−1, τ). After pretraining the obstacle map network Gϕ, we freeze it during semantic map network ˜Gϕ training and cease further updates. ˜Gϕ integrates obstacle map information via an obstacle-aware feature modulation network. Specifically, as shown in Fig. 2 (b), given the k-th feature map f k τ , we adapt feature map ˆf kτ in ˜Gϕ using a spatially-adaptive denormalization (Park et al., 2019) residual block: Label Map Restored. Fig. 2 (a) illustrates the PLMD pipeline for a single robot. In the multi-robot setting, the same pipeline is executed independently by each robot on its own observations and map state. In single robot pipeline, each robot processes its current RGB-D view ot, sensor posi- tion pt, and Goal G to construct semantic and obstacle map vectors. We use a fixed palette to populate the label indexes, resulting in a visualized semantic map Svt and a visualized obstacle map Cvt. For efficiency, these maps are cropped
title: Plug-and-Play Label Map Diffusion for Universal Goal-Oriented Navigation
visual_description:
1. The figure, titled "Plug-and-Play Label Map Dilation for Universal Goal-Oriented Navigation", is divided into two main parts labeled "(a)" and "(b)". Panel (a), on the left, shows the goal-conditioned navigation architecture that processes an RGB-D observation, robot pose, goal information, semantic labels, and obstacle labels. Panel (b), on the right, shows the plug-and-play label-map dilation procedure, including obstacle masking, a dilation model "DM", noise estimation, conditioning, and generation of a refined semantic map.

2. At the top of panel (a), the goal specification can be either an "Object" or an "Image", represented by corresponding icons. This goal input defines "Goal G_t^l". To its right, an "Action" block depicts the four discrete navigation directions: forward, backward, left, and right. The goal and action information are connected to the navigation pipeline by solid black paths.

3. The main sensory input in panel (a) is an indoor RGB-D frame labeled "RGB-D Observation". Multiple layered copies behind the frame indicate a sequence or stack of observations. A separate lower input labeled "Robot Pose" is also supplied to the architecture. The observation and pose streams enter the large blue navigation-model region.

4. The RGB-D observation is encoded into several intermediate spatial feature maps, illustrated by small gray map images and a larger blue feature tensor with multiple channels. Blue arrows connect these representations to the convolutional processing stack and to the semantic and obstacle prediction branches.

5. The central feature-processing path contains repeated blocks labeled "3*3 Conv", "ReLU", and "SPADE". The SPADE modules condition the convolutional feature transformations on spatial label-map information. Ellipses between blocks indicate that additional repeated convolutional stages are omitted from the drawing. The stack feeds upward into the "Navigation Strategy" module.

6. A blue addition node marked "+" combines feature information with a pose-dependent signal associated with "Localization Strategy". A recurrent black loop beside the navigation module indicates temporal state propagation. The visible state notation includes c_t and a transformed or recurrent feature f_tau^k. An orange dashed feedback path supplies predicted-map information to the SPADE-conditioned processing stages.

7. Two parallel prediction modules receive encoded visual features: "Semantic Labeling" predicts semantic categories, and "Obstacles Labeling" predicts obstacle occupancy. Their outputs are drawn as stacks of grid tensors. The semantic tensor is labeled "n*H*W", indicating n semantic channels over an H by W map, while the obstacle tensor is labeled "2*H*W", indicating two obstacle channels over the same spatial dimensions.

8. The semantic and obstacle tensors are combined at a blue "+" node, with the operation labeled "concatenate". The resulting map is visualized as a color-coded semantic floor map. The semantic output uses multiple class colors, while obstacle or free-space information is represented separately in grayscale. A small vertical color strip and the label "Predicted Label Map" identify the class-map output that is fed back into the navigation network.

9. Panel (b) expands the map-processing portion of the system. A visualized predicted semantic label map, denoted s_t^P, is shown with colored spatial regions corresponding to semantic classes. Blue dotted callout lines link the smaller predicted map to a larger visualization, indicating enlargement rather than a separate processing operation.

10. The obstacle branch includes an "Obstacles Palette" with two displayed values, black and gray, corresponding to the two channels of the 2*H*W obstacle prediction. Applying this palette produces the grayscale "Visualized Obstacles Map C_t^0". The map distinguishes obstacle or unknown regions from navigable regions.

11. A blue masking operation labeled "Mask C_t^m" is applied to the obstacle-map representation. The masked grayscale map is passed downward through the block labeled "DM". The output of DM is labeled "Noise" and enters a blue subtraction node marked "-". This mask-and-noise path is enclosed by a gray dashed boundary, identifying it as a distinct dilation or correction subsystem.

12. The subtraction result is used as a "Condition" for the lower noise-estimation module. This module is labeled "Noise sigma_t^0" and is depicted as a neural network with a sequence of vertical feature bars. The associated formula is shown as g_tilde_phi(s_t^m, c_t^(tau-1), tau), indicating a model parameterized by phi that operates on the masked map s_t^m, a previous-step condition c_t^(tau-1), and diffusion or iteration index tau.

13. The conditioned dilation process produces a large color-coded output labeled "Masked Map s_t^m". Compared with the sparse or incomplete predicted semantic map, this map contains expanded semantic regions within the navigable layout while retaining black masked areas. Blue dotted connectors indicate the correspondence between the predicted map, the selected region, and the enlarged masked-map result.

14. Orange dotted paths around the lower portion of the figure indicate iterative feedback across dilation steps. Labels involving tau, including f_tau^k and c_t^(tau-1), mark the step-dependent features and conditioning variables. These paths return the refined map information toward the convolutional and SPADE blocks, allowing the plug-and-play dilation result to influence subsequent navigation processing.

15. Overall, panel (a) predicts actions from object- or image-goal information, RGB-D observations, robot pose, semantic labels, and obstacle labels. Panel (b) takes the predicted semantic and obstacle maps, constructs an obstacle mask, estimates and removes noise with DM and the conditioned noise model, and returns a spatially dilated label map for continued goal-oriented navigation.
